title: ml.get_buckets
description:
Get anomaly detection job results for buckets.

The API presents a chronological view of the records, grouped by bucket.

anomaly_score.description: Refer to the description for the `anomaly_score` query parameter.

desc.description: Refer to the description for the `desc` query parameter.

end.description: Refer to the description for the `end` query parameter.

exclude_interim.description: Refer to the description for the `exclude_interim` query parameter.

expand.description: Refer to the description for the `expand` query parameter.

from.description: Skips the specified number of buckets.

size.description: Specifies the maximum number of buckets to obtain.

sort.description: Refer to the desription for the `sort` query parameter.

start.description: Refer to the description for the `start` query parameter.

job_id.description: Identifier for the anomaly detection job.

timestamp.description:
The timestamp of a single bucket result. If you do not specify this
parameter, the API returns information about all buckets.

error_trace.description:
When set to `true` Elasticsearch will include the full stack trace of errors
when they occur.

filter_path.description:
Comma-separated list of filters in dot notation which reduce the response
returned by Elasticsearch.

human.description:
When set to `true` will return statistics in a format suitable for humans.
For example `"exists_time": "1h"` for humans and
`"exists_time_in_millis": 3600000` for computers. When disabled the human
readable values will be omitted. This makes sense for responses being consumed
only by machines.

pretty.description:
If set to `true` the returned JSON will be "pretty-formatted". Only use
this option for debugging only.
